newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya urges Mandela not to sell arms to Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: Kenya urges Mandela not to sell arms to Rwanda.

text.p: Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi on Sunday urged South African President Nelson Mandela to suspend all arms sales to Rwanda until Rwandan troops withdrew from eastern Zaire, the presidency said.

Moi told Mandela in a telephone conversation that "it would be prudent for South Africa to suspend any further sales of arms to Rwanda until Rwandan troops were withdrawn from Zairean territory", the presidential press service (PPS) said.
"President Moi pointed out that this would forestall an escalation of the fighting going on in eastern Zaire," it said.
Tutsi rebels have captured a string of towns in eastern Zaire bordering Rwanda and Burundi in an offensive launched last month.
Zaire accuses Rwandan troops of fighting alongside the rebels inside Zaire and has ruled out peace talks until they leave. Rwanda denies the charge.

The PPS added that Moi and Mandela discussed a summit Moi has called for Nairobi on Tuesday to seek an end to the fighting in Zaire. Moi also briefed Mandela about sanctions regional countries have imposed on Burundi.
Kenyan officials said on Thursday Moi would meet the leaders of Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, Rwanda, Ethiopia and Cameroon in Nairobi on Tuesday.
